_about: Classification rules per commodity, on true surface reflectance (Sentinel-2's +1000 offset removed). Each was set from index values sampled over the 2023 NAIP photo of a yard and checked by outlining the result on that photo (tools/calibrate.py). A pixel is water if NDWI > water_ndwi and NIR < water_nir_max; vegetation if NDVI > veg_ndvi; stockpile if it is neither and brightness is inside [brightness_min, brightness_max] and every other *_min / *_max test named here passes (bsi, warmth = (red-blue)/(red+blue), saturation, swir1). green_ever_ndvi: pixels whose 90th-percentile NDVI over all clear scenes is above this are seasonal vegetation (summer-dry grass looks like logs) and never count. min_object_px drops specks smaller than that many 10 m pixels; fill_holes_px fills gaps inside a pile up to that size. subtract_persistent: ground that reads as stockpile on nearly every clear date (white roofs, slabs) is kept out of the active area; off for container yards, which are full nearly every day. Pixels that are white in the visible but dark in SWIR (NDSI > 0.4) are snow; scenes with more than 20% of the yard under snow, or with the yard's blue band 1.5x brighter than usual (missed cloud, smoke), are set aside.

lumber.label: Logs, lumber and chips
lumber.why: Fresh wood, bark and chips are warm-coloured (red well above blue); pavement and roofs are grey, and the dark bark mud between the decks falls under the brightness floor. Summer-dry grass is the same colour, which the seasonal-green test removes. Wet wood darkens, so winter areas read lower: compare like seasons.

containers.label: Container stacks
containers.why: Stacked boxes are mostly red, orange and brown paint, so much warmer than the grey pavement around them. Blue and white boxes are missed, so this is an index of how full the stacks are, not a box count.

wind_components.label: Wind turbine blades and towers
wind_components.why: Blades are white and neutral: brighter than the yard pavement and with no warm tint. White roofs match too, which is what the persistent-ground subtraction removes.
